SM_Cottage_Stonebrook_PR.known_weaknesses: Thatch is now four slope planes with a rounded 0.4 m eaves roll, a 5 cm course ledge every 0.36 m, combed streaks, hollows, moss on the north pitch and ridge, hip rolls and a block ridge with three liggers a side; still faulted: the 0.54 m scan period shows close up; ledges are evenly spaced (real coats wander more); hip rolls are plain sweeps; no netting; the eaves butt is a smooth cut. Earth apron and flagstones are part of the mesh: its edge is a mesh edge against the terrain (vertex-colour green helps, it is not a blend). Door leaf is fixed ajar at 62 degrees (not a separate hinged object here; SM_Cottage_Door_PR is). The room behind the door is an unlit black face 0.3 m in. Jamb and quoin stones carry the rubble scan scaled, not single-stone textures. Rafter-pole feet are evenly spaced stubs. Bounds are not centred on the pivot any more (apron and flagstones reach 2.6 m in front): validator PIVOT by design, the pivot is still the centre of the 18 x 9 m walls. 77,000 triangles (soft target 60,000, hard 200,000).

SM_Cottage_Thatched_Small_PR.status: same generator as the Stonebrook cottage; one render per round, not three own rounds
SM_Cottage_Thatched_Small_PR.known_weaknesses: As SM_Cottage_Stonebrook_PR. Sized by judgement from the oblique sprite, no doorway (the original places the door as its own sprite). The ridge is only about 1.5 m long, so the block ridge is a short saddle.

SM_Cottage_Thatched_Large_PR.status: same generator as the Stonebrook cottage; one render per round, not three own rounds
SM_Cottage_Thatched_Large_PR.known_weaknesses: As SM_Cottage_Stonebrook_PR. Sized by judgement from the oblique sprite, no doorway (the original places the door as its own sprite). Also bound to cottage_thatched_long.

SM_Cottage_Door_PR.known_weaknesses: The town door leaf at 1.44 x 2.46 m: plank scan repeats across planks; studs are plain bevelled squares. Validator UV_OVERLAP by design (tiling library planks).

SM_Fence_SplitRail_4m_PR.known_weaknesses: Rails are six-sided wedge sweeps: knots and splits come only from the oak scan, not from geometry; lichen and moss are vertex-colour blends; post tops are plain tapers; lashings are a helix with the straw scan as fibre, no knot. Validator UV_OVERLAP by design (tiling library materials).

SM_Fence_Gate_PR.known_weaknesses: Stiles are straight boxes; bars are not visibly mortised; hinges are flat straps without a forged eye. Validator UV_OVERLAP by design.

SM_Fence_GatePost_PR.known_weaknesses: Very simple (462 triangles): a tapered seven-sided post, two pins, four stones. Validator UV_OVERLAP by design.

SM_Well_Stone_PR.known_weaknesses: Real shaft to -3.7 m with dark water at -3.45 m: needs a hole in the ground (see fit) or SM_Well_ShaftCap_PR. The water is an opaque dark glossy disc (no transparency, no ripple); it is hard to see from the game camera. Wet moss and the rope-worn capstone are vertex-colour blends, no cut grooves. Stones are displaced icospheres (320 triangles each), rounded, no tool marks. Roof shingles are the oak board scan turned down the slope. Validator: UV_OVERLAP by design; PIVOT by design (the mesh goes below the ground pivot). 20,400 triangles.

SM_Boulder_Field_A_PR.status: rebuilt in round 3 as a unique bake; two review rounds
SM_Boulder_Field_A_PR.known_weaknesses: Unique bake from a 20k-triangle fractured source: bedding ledges are too regular (reads as a stack of beds on every side), split faces are soft-edged after decimation, lichen rosettes are small and sparse from the game camera, the soil skirt is a baked tint (no modelled soil or grass). 1.90 x 1.40 x 1.15 m: about 10 % smaller in plan than the old SM_Boulder_Fieldstone_01 (2.12 x 1.69 x 1.19 m).

SM_Cottage_Stonebrook_PR_Burnt.status: new in round 3; two review rounds (sb4, sb5) and the final render, not three full rounds
SM_Cottage_Stonebrook_PR_Burnt.known_weaknesses: Rafters, laths and fallen timbers are charred six-sided poles with little break-up: no alligator cracking, no burnt-through sections, laths read as a ladder. The surviving thatch ends in a ragged but clean-cut black edge, no hanging straw. Heaps of burnt thatch and ash are smooth domes. Soot is a vertex-colour layer (0.2 m): plumes above openings are soft. Walls are intact to full height (no fallen masonry, no spalled stones). The fallen door is the intact leaf blackened. No embers, smoke or glow (emitters). Collision keeps the intact walls. 63,000 triangles.

SM_Fence_SplitRail_4m_Broken_PR.known_weaknesses: As the intact run; the snapped rail ends are tapered points, not splintered breaks.

SM_Well_ShaftCap_PR.known_weaknesses: a black disc; only for places where the ground cannot be cut

contract.uv: UV0 already carries the tiling: one UV unit is one repeat of the set (tile_size_m is the nominal size the UVs were laid out for; small blocks use up to 2x denser UVs). Sample BC, N, ORM and H at UV0; sample Macro at UV0 / 7. Do not rescale.
contract.textures: BC sRGB; N linear OpenGL (flip green on import); ORM linear (R ambient occlusion, G roughness, B metallic = 0); H linear 16-bit height, used 0..1; Macro linear 512 px (R large, G medium, B small variation).
contract.vertex_colour: FBX vertex colour set 'Grime', linear RGBA float, exported with every LOD. R = dirt and damp, G = moss / algae, B = bleaching (silvered oak, lichen, dressed stone, fresh straw), A = material switch (see below; 1 everywhere else).
graph: base = BC * tint * (1 - macro + 2 * macro * Macro.R)
dirt_mode multiply: c = lerp(base, base * dirt, fd * dirt_amount);   dirt_mode mix: c = lerp(base, dirt * (3 * luminance(base) + 0.35), fd * dirt_amount)
fb = saturate(B * saturate(0.9 * H + 0.35));   c = lerp(c, pale * (2.2 * luminance(c) + 0.55), fb * pale_amount)
fm = saturate(4 * ((G + 0.5 * Macro.B) - (0.55 * H + 0.62))) * (G > 0.02);   c = lerp(c, moss * (0.9 * Macro.G + 0.55), fm)
roughness = lerp(ORM.G, moss_roughness, fm) - 0.10 * fd;   normal = N;   metallic = 0

alpha_switch materials only: A < 0.875 lead (only where alpha_lead is true): colour (0.15, 0.16, 0.17) * (0.7 * Macro.G + 0.65), roughness 0.42, flat normal;  A < 0.625 (A < 0.75 where alpha_lead is false) black iron, charred wood, burnt straw or unlit void: colour (0.016, 0.015, 0.014), roughness 0.5 + 0.42 * R (iron has R = 0, char has R = 1), normal kept;  A < 0.25 window glass: colour glass_tint, roughness 0.06, flat normal, opaque (the pane mesh is faceted so each quarry reflects differently; a dark closed box stands behind it). Values written: 1, 0.75, 0.5, 0.
alpha_soot materials only: fs = saturate((1 - A) * (0.7 * Macro.G + 1.0));  c = lerp(c, (0.012, 0.011, 0.010), fs);  roughness = lerp(roughness, 0.97, fs)
contract.fbx: One FBX per asset beside the manifest: mesh objects <asset>_LOD0, _LOD1, _LOD2 (import as one static mesh with three LODs) and UCX_<asset>_LOD0_NN convex hulls; metres with UnitScaleFactor 100; Z up, front -Y; smoothing by edge (import normals); material slots in the order of each module's "materials" list. Family meshes are visual only (ART_STANDARD section 5).
